commitResults.messageBody:
Ui.showMessage() previously took a single String and was unused.
Changed it to showMessage(String... lines) so it can print a variable
number of related lines in one call, and replaced the repeated
System.out.println blocks in Lion.main() (task-added, mark/unmark,
delete, find, and error messages) with calls to it. Reduces
duplication and gives showMessage() an actual purpose.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assertions for parser assumptions
commitResults.messageBody:
Add assertions to verify expected command types, required parsed
values, and valid arguments passed to parser helper methods. This
helps detect violations of internal parser assumptions during
development.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove duplicated command-handling logic between CLI and GUI
commitResults.messageBody:
Lion.main() and Lion.getResponse() each contained a full, separate
switch statement implementing every command (todo, deadline, event,
mark, unmark, delete, find), so every change to a command's behavior
had to be made twice and could silently drift out of sync. This
violates the DRY guideline in the code quality guide ("Minimize Code
Duplication ... duplicated code signals design issues") and also made
main() a 190-line method, far past the guide's "avoid long methods"
threshold.

main() now builds a Lion instance and delegates entirely to
getResponse() for command handling, adding only the CLI's four-space
message margin via the new indentForCli() helper. As a side effect,
this also removes an inconsistency in error handling: previously a
failed save was reported to the user on the CLI but silently ignored
on the GUI (an empty catch block, which the guide flags under "avoid
unsafe shortcuts"); saveTasks() now returns a failure notice that is
appended to the response on both paths.

Because the CLI's per-line indentation was applied uniformly (all
lines get the same four-space margin) rather than case-by-case, a few
lines that previously had one or two extra leading spaces (e.g. the
task line under "Got it. I've added this task:") are now indented
consistently with the rest of the box; this is a minor, intentional
side effect of unifying the two implementations, not a functional
change.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract magic number 100 into TaskList.MAX_TASKS constant
commitResults.messageBody:
The task-array capacity of 100 was hardcoded as an unexplained numeric
literal in two separate places: TaskList's no-arg constructor and
Storage.loadTaskList(). This is exactly the "Avoid Magic Numbers" case
from the code quality guide (an unexplained literal that should be a
named constant), and duplicating it in two files meant the two array
sizes could drift out of sync if only one were ever updated.

Introduce TaskList.MAX_TASKS as the single named source of truth for
this capacity, and have Storage.loadTaskList() reference it instead of
repeating the literal.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename misleading tmp variable in DialogBox.flip()
commitResults.messageBody:
The code quality guide explicitly calls out "temp" as a bad variable
name under "Use Names to Explain": a name should describe what a
variable holds, not just note that it's temporary (nearly every local
variable is, in that sense). Here it held the dialog box's children in
reversed order, so name it reversedChildren to make that purpose clear
at the point of use.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract magic numbers for minimum window size in Main.java
commitResults.messageBody:
stage.setMinHeight(220) and stage.setMinWidth(417) used unexplained
numeric literals, which the code quality guide flags under "Avoid
Magic Numbers": a reader has no way to tell what 220 or 417 mean, or
whether the two calls are related, without inspecting the surrounding
context. Naming them MIN_WINDOW_HEIGHT and MIN_WINDOW_WIDTH makes
their purpose clear at the call site.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract command-prefix lengths in Parser into named constants
commitResults.messageBody:
Each Parser method skipped a hardcoded number of characters to strip
its command word (substring(4), substring(9), substring(5), ...), and
Lion.java separately hardcoded the same numbers (5, 7) when calling
getTaskIndex(). These are unexplained numeric literals — the "Avoid
Magic Numbers" case from the code quality guide — and having the same
values duplicated across two files meant they could silently drift out
of sync if a command word ever changed.

Give each command-prefix length its own named constant on Parser
(public where Lion.java needs to reference it for getTaskIndex, private
otherwise), and update both Parser's own methods and Lion.java's call
sites to use them instead of the raw numbers. The assert in
getTaskIndex now checks against MARK_PREFIX_LENGTH and
UNMARK_OR_DELETE_PREFIX_LENGTH directly rather than restating their
values.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove obvious/stray inline comments in Storage.load()
commitResults.messageBody:
// turn into task object next to tasks[count] = decode(line) restates
exactly what the code already says, which the guide flags under "Do
Not Repeat the Obvious" (its own example: //increment x above x++).
// T | 1 | buy boook next to scanner.nextLine() was a stray example
left over from development (misspelled, and written as a note to self
rather than for a reader), which the guide flags under "Write to the
Reader": comments should explain something a reader of the finished
code needs, not record what the author was looking at.

The save-line format that comment illustrated is genuinely useful
information, so it now lives once, correctly, in decode()'s Javadoc
(which is the method that actually defines and depends on that
format) instead of being repeated informally at every call site.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain the silent date-parse fallback in Deadline's constructor
commitResults.messageBody:
The catch block that falls back to LocalDateTime.now() on an
unparseable date had no comment explaining why the parse failure is
swallowed instead of surfaced. The guide's "Avoid Empty Catch Blocks"
rule allows silently handling an exception only "if unavoidable, [with
an] explanatory comment" — this catch wasn't literally empty, but it
had the same problem: a reader had no way to tell whether the silent
fallback was a deliberate design decision or an oversight.

Document the actual reason: this constructor is also invoked by
Storage.decode() while loading the save file, so throwing here would
prevent the whole task list from loading over one bad line, which is
why "now" is used as a resilient fallback instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Separate getStatusIcon() and getDescription() with a blank line
commitResults.messageBody:
getStatusIcon()'s closing brace was directly followed by the next
method's Javadoc with no blank line between them, unlike every other
method boundary in this file. The guide's "Structure Code Logically"
section calls for using blank lines to group and separate logical
units so the code reads clearly; this was a one-off inconsistency
against the rest of the class.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document DialogBox factory methods and rename var db
commitResults.messageBody:
getUserDialog() and getLionDialog() are the only two public factory
methods used by the rest of the GUI, but had no Javadoc explaining
what each one produces or why getLionDialog also flips the layout;
this project follows the SE-EDU coding standard, which the code
quality guide points to under "Follow a Standard", and that standard
requires Javadoc on public methods other than trivial getters/setters.

Also rename the local `var db` to `DialogBox dialogBox`: "db" reads as
an abbreviation for "database" out of context, and `var` was not used
anywhere else in the codebase, so spelling out the type keeps this
method consistent with the rest of the project's style.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename setLion's cryptic parameter and document initialize()
commitResults.messageBody:
setLion(Lion l) used a single-letter parameter name, so the assignment
lion = l; read ambiguously; renaming the parameter to lion and writing
this.lion = lion follows the same shadowing convention already used
throughout the rest of the codebase (e.g. Task's constructor). This
follows the code quality guide's naming guidance to use names that
explain a value's purpose rather than the shortest name that compiles.

initialize() is a public method with no Javadoc; it is an FXML
lifecycle callback by naming convention, not an actual method override,
so it isn't covered by the SE-EDU standard's exception for overrides
and needs its own explanation like any other public method.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use a Stream to implement TaskList.find()
commitResults.messageBody:
find() filtered the backing array by hand with an index-based for
loop and an if-check that only ever did one thing (add the task to
the result). This is exactly a filter-then-collect operation, which
java.util.stream expresses more directly: stream() -> filter(...) ->
forEach(matches::add).

Added TaskList.stream() (backed by Arrays.stream(tasks, 0, size), so
it only exposes the active tasks, never the unused capacity) as a
small reusable building block other classes can use for read-only
traversal of the list, rather than exposing the raw array.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use a Stream to build LIST/FIND's numbered task listing
commitResults.messageBody:
The LIST and FIND cases each built their numbered output with an
almost identical index-based for loop appending to a StringBuilder,
differing only in the header text and which TaskList they numbered.
Replaced both with a single formatNumberedList(TaskList) helper using
IntStream.range(...).mapToObj(...).collect(Collectors.joining()),
which both expresses "map each index to a line, then join" more
directly than the loop did and removes the duplication between the
two cases.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use a Stream to indent CLI responses line-by-line
commitResults.messageBody:
indentForCli() manually allocated a same-size output array and copied
each line into it with a prefixed margin via an index-based loop. This
is a plain one-to-one transformation of a sequence, which
Arrays.stream(...).map(...).toArray(String[]::new) expresses directly
without the manual array bookkeeping.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use a Stream to build the save-file content in Storage.save()
commitResults.messageBody:
save() wrote each task with two separate write() calls inside a
manual index-based loop. Built the whole file content as one string
via Arrays.stream(tasks, 0, taskCount).map(...).collect(...) instead,
so encode() is applied uniformly across the active tasks and the only
remaining call that can throw IOException is the single write() at
the end.

Used task -> encode(task) + System.lineSeparator() joined with no
delimiter (rather than Collectors.joining with a separator/suffix) so
that zero tasks still produce an entirely empty string, matching the
original loop's behavior exactly; a joining()-with-suffix approach
would instead write one stray blank line for an empty task list, which
Storage.decode() cannot parse.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a help command that lists all available commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Users had no in-app way to see what commands exist or what they do;
the only feedback for a typo or unfamiliar syntax was "I don't know
what that means", with no pointer to how to find out. Add a bare
`help` command that lists every command with a one-line description.

Give each CommandType enum constant a real description field/getter
instead of writing a second, separate block of command descriptions
in Lion.java: the enum's Javadoc already documents each command's
purpose, and a hand-written duplicate paragraph would drift out of
sync with it over time. Lion.getResponse()'s new HELP case streams
over CommandType.values() (skipping UNKNOWN, which isn't a command a
user can type) to build the listing, so adding a future command to
the enum keeps the help page correct automatically.

Also point the existing "I don't know what that means" message at the
new command, so users who hit it have an obvious next step.

Both go through getResponse(), so the CLI and GUI share this for free
with no separate plumbing, following the single-implementation
pattern from branch-A-CodeQuality.

Added LionTest (none existed before) covering the new help listing
and the updated unknown-command message, plus a CommandTypeTest case
confirming "help" resolves to CommandType.HELP.
